title: Leveraging machine learning to uncover multi-pathogen infection dynamics across co-distributed frog families
summary: Among 1,281 sampled frogs, about 20% had at least one pathogen detected. Ranidae accounted for 74.3% of infections and had higher Bd intensity than the other two families. RF models identified host species and temperature-linked variables as key predictors; Bd/Rv infections were associated with higher latitudes and cooler, more stable temperatures, while Perkinsea trends differed. Three pathogens were screened/quantified by qPCR. RF models used overfitting checks, cross-validation and repeated 70/30 train/test splits (100 iterations); infection-status models covered up to 1,281 samples, with a 216-sample Bd intensity model. Results are observational and non-causal; the paper cautions about small positive groups/overfitting and does not sample across seasons.
ai_technology: Balanced random-forest classification/regression models predicted infection status and intensity from host taxonomy, age, sex, geography and environmental variables; variable importance plus one-way analyses identified pathogen-specific predictors.
